typesafe.notes: Provider of the typed decision routes dm.hosted and dm.hosted.preview. account_status is the one field that opens or closes every route naming this provider at once, and it is declared as data rather than assumed in code because code that assumed an account existed would be asserting something nobody measured: the loader admits no route whose provider is not live, so a key sitting in the environment is inert until this file says the account is open. It is live, and the account answers: the organisation-scoped key named by api_key_env returns a typed answer from the endpoint below. The key is never in this file — api_key_env names the variable it is read from on every call and secret_path says where it is kept — so opening a provider is a reviewed release of this package and never a runtime act. The vendor's own posture on the image and box surface it serves here is a durable property of that surface and not a remark about a moment in its history: it calls them "Dreamer-ready", states that they "aren't yet up to our standards to call ready for production", and warns that "the request format, the answers, and the limits on this page can change between releases". That is why the headers reaching those surfaces are per-call opt-ins a caller names, and nothing this table turns on. model_aliases records the two moving names the vendor publishes and the versioned id each resolves to, each confirmed by an authenticated call rather than read: a request naming jev-latest is answered by jev-1.13.0 and one naming jev-preview by jev-1.14.0, and the response reports the resolved versioned id rather than the name that was sent. They are recorded and never sent, because an alias moves when a release ships, so sending one would change the answering model with no change on this side; the loader refuses a pin that ends in either name, and re-pointing an entry here is a reviewed edit of this file that changes no request. GET /v1/models lists these two aliases and no versioned id, and a versioned id is accepted by the model field whether or not it appears in that list — the vendor states so and an authenticated call confirms it — so that list is the set of names an account may send and never the set of ids a route may pin. The base URL is the one the vendor's API reference and SDK default to.

engine-judge.notes: A checkpoint the consumer loads and serves in a process of its own. This package declares it so every consumer reads one table, and holds no transport for it: it has no URL and no key name here because nothing in this package addresses or authenticates against it. pending-onboarding until the consumer's serving process exists.

dm.hosted.notes: Pinned to the versioned id the models page lists for Jev 1.13, never to jev-latest or jev-preview: the same page says an alias "moves when a new release ships, so the answers behind it can change without a change on your side". The pin is confirmed from both ends — the models page lists jev-1.13.0, and an authenticated call naming it is answered by it, while a call naming jev-latest reports jev-1.13.0 as the model that answered. contract_evidence is authenticated-call and contract_verified is the day the request, response and error shapes were exercised against the live endpoint with the organisation's key, rather than read from the reference: a 200 carrying the typed answers, the usage counts and the answering model, and a 400 whose body is {"detail":{"error_type","message"}} for a model id the account cannot send. An id the vendor does not serve comes back 400 "Unknown model", so a pin written here is validated by the vendor and never silently passed through. Caps are the documented ones: "a maximum of 255 options per Choice" and a Score that "accepts up to 10" levels; the models page states that "There is no separate limit on the number of questions in a request", so max_questions is null. supports_box is false because the vendor states "Box questions need Jev 1.14": images are accepted on both models, and the question that locates something in one is served by the newer alone, so a box sent here is refused before it is paid for. The models page's capability table reads "Input: Text" for both releases while the images page states that both accept images; the two vendor pages disagree, the specific page governs, and an authenticated call carrying a PNG is answered, so images are accepted on this route. Price is the models page's $0.042 per 1M input tokens with "Output tokens are free"; an image is billed as ordinary input tokens at that price and the vendor publishes no way to estimate how many of them an image costs, so no cost model for an image is stated here. What was measured is that the count follows the canvas and not the file: a 25 KB chart and a 4 KB blank at the same 1024x768 canvas were billed the same 2632 input tokens. Two numbers on this route are free parameters, to be narrowed by measurement and never guessed. budget_ms 1500 is a ceiling and not an operating point: about three times the longest latency measured on these routes, which is a band and not a point: a read over one 1024x768 PNG has measured 468 to 515 ms across two and three questions, and a one-question text call 281 to 313 ms and well under the vendor SDK's 10000 ms per-attempt default; the consumer's own deadline for a typed step is what a call actually runs under. max_state_tokens 32000 is the documented ceiling for the state plus the longest question ("64k tokens per request; 32k tokens for state plus the longest question"), an upper bound and not a target: a state shared across routes is bound by the smallest ceiling among them. defaults.circuit_breaker (5 failures, 60000 ms cooldown, 15000 ms capacity cooldown, 1 half-open probe, no latency trip) is carried from the generative alias table and has not been measured against this vendor. max_state_tokens is the DEFAULT ceiling. The vendor raises both of its context limits to 262000 tokens for a request sent with its long-context header, which works on both releases and which this package sends only when a call names that surface; the vendor states that long context "is slower and less accurate than staying within the default limits", so the default is what the table declares and the raised ceiling is a per-call fact a caller that opts in already holds.

dm.hosted.preview.notes: The vendor's newest release, pinned to the versioned id its models page lists for Jev 1.14 and never to the moving name that currently points at it; an authenticated call naming jev-preview reports jev-1.14.0 as the model that answered, so the name and the pin are confirmed to resolve to the same model and the pin is what is sent. It exists as a route of its own rather than as a model a caller could name on dm.hosted, because a route IS its pinned model together with the caps, budget and price that model is served under: a caller able to choose the model could move the answering model without a reviewed change to this file. The vendor raises both of its context limits to 262000 tokens for a request sent with its long-context header, which works on both releases and which this package sends only when a call names that surface; the vendor states that long context "is slower and less accurate than staying within the default limits", so the default is what the table declares and the raised ceiling is a per-call fact a caller that opts in already holds.

dm.local.notes: Declared here and answered by the consumer's own process; this package refuses to serve it. The checkpoint is the English one, loaded with laya 0.3.22 at the Hugging Face revision that was the head when the model card was read. artifact_sha256 is null and pin_status is pending-artifact-digests because no per-artifact SHA-256 has been recorded anywhere: a digest is transcribed from the downloaded artifact, never written from memory, and the consumer refuses to serve the checkpoint until the map is filled. max_state_tokens 320 is what the model card leaves for state in the English checkpoint's 512-token window once 192 tokens are reserved for the question and its options. max_options 20 is where the card says options start to be trimmed to fit ("around 20 options with a short description each"); max_score_levels 32 and max_questions 64 are the serving package's own request limits. budget_ms 1000 is a free parameter: it sits above the card's 771 ms for 50 questions on a T4 GPU and is a ceiling the consumer's deadline narrows. A CPU replay does not fit inside it (580 ms for one question on a 4-core server CPU) and is the consumer's concern. price_per_mtok is null because the route bills nothing per token.
